summary: Alfred Forke worked in sinology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Geneva (~1886–1887) and the University of Berlin (~1887–1889), and held posts at the Seminar für Orientalische Sprachen zu Berlin (1903–1923) and the University of Hamburg (~1923–1935).

Alfred Foucher worked in Indology, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the École Normale Supérieure and under Sylvain Lévi at the EPHE, later holding positions at the EFEO, the EPHE, and the University of Paris (1907; 1929–1936).

Alfred Gell studied at the University of Cambridge under Edmund Leach and completed his Ph.D. at the London School of Economics. He later held posts at the University of Sussex, the Australian National University, and the London School of Economics.

Alfred Hillebrandt was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at the University of Breslau under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler and at the University of Munich under Martin Haug, later holding a chair at Breslau from 1887 to 1921.

Alfred Körte specialized in history, archaeology, and linguistics. After studying at the University of Bonn (~1886–1890), he held academic posts at the universities of Bonn, Greifswald, Basel, Giessen, Freiburg, and Leipzig (~1917–1934).

Alfred Ludwig worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Vienna and Berlin, learning Sanskrit under Albrecht Weber and studying under Friedrich Müller, Moriz Haupt, and others. He later served as professor of comparative linguistics at the University of Prague.

Alfred Radcliffe-Brown was educated at Trinity College, Cambridge (~1901–1905). He held academic posts at the University of Sydney (~1926–1931), the University of Chicago (~1931–1937), the University of Oxford (~1937–1946), and FESP in São Paulo.
Ali Asani works in religious studies and Indology, serving on the faculty at Harvard University and on the editorial board of Perspectives on Islamicate South Asia.

Linguist Alice Harris studied at the University of Massachusetts Amherst and Harvard University (~1973–1976). She held long-term faculty posts at Vanderbilt University (~1979–2009) and the University of Massachusetts Amherst (~2009).

Alicia Turner works in Buddhist and religious studies. She completed her PhD at the University of Chicago, supervised by Bruce Lincoln and Steven Collins, and also studied with Saw Tun, Daw Than Than Win, John Okell, and Carol S. Anderson.

Alison Denton Jones works in religious studies, sinology, and Buddhist studies. Her doctoral supervisor was Martin King Whyte, and she also studied under Allan H. Barr, Mingfei Gao, and Margaret Dornish.

Alka Patel specializes in history, archaeology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She studied at Mount Holyoke College and completed her PhD at Harvard University before becoming an associate professor at the University of California, Irvine.

Allan G. Grapard specialized in Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He earned his Ph.D. at INALCO and was a professor of Shinto studies and East Asian studies at the University of California, Santa Barbara.

Allan Gibbard is a philosopher who studied at Swarthmore College and Harvard University. He held faculty posts at the University of Chicago (1969–1974), the University of Pittsburgh (1974–1977), and the University of Michigan (1977–2016).
Allan H. Barr is a sinologist who earned his doctorate from the University of Oxford in 1983. He held a post as Professor of Asian Languages and Literatures at Pomona College.

Allen Wright Thrasher is an Indologist who completed his doctoral studies under Daniel H. H. Ingalls, alongside traditional teachers in India. He served at the Library of Congress from around 1983 to 2011.
Alnis Dickson studied Buddhist studies and Tibetology at McGill University, completing an MA supervised by Lara Braitstein, and also studied under G. Victor Sōgen Hori.

Alois Anton Führer worked in Indology and archaeology after completing a PhD at the University of Würzburg under Julius Jolly. He held posts at the Archaeological Survey of India, the State Museum, Lucknow, and St. Xavier's College, Mumbai.
Alois Müller worked in linguistics and librarianship. He held posts at Palacký University Olomouc (1874–1879), Graz University Library (director, 1879), and Vienna University Library (~1867–1901).

Aloys Sprenger studied at Vienna under Joseph von Hammer-Purgstall and at Leiden. He served as principal of Delhi College and Aliah University, secretary of The Asiatic Society, and professor of oriental languages at the University of Bern (1857–1881).
